slides.title: THE KILOMETRES
slides.head: Most shoes are worn out somewhere around 500 to 800 km.
slides.body: Lighter racing shoes often go sooner. Log your shoes in your watch app so you know.

slides.title: IT FEELS FLAT
slides.head: The bounce has gone.
slides.body: If your easy runs suddenly feel harder on your legs, the foam may have given up before the upper did.

slides.title: BALD SOLES
slides.head: Smooth patches mean less grip.
slides.body: Check the heel and forefoot. Worn rubber slips on wet roads and loose trail.

slides.title: NEW NIGGLES
slides.head: Aches that weren't there last month.
slides.body: Nothing else changed in your training? Your shoes might have. Ease off and see someone if it hangs around.

slides.title: YOU LOVE THEM
slides.head: Favourite shoes get kept too long.
slides.body: Buy the next pair early and run them in on short runs, so you're never stuck in a dead pair before a race.
